judged_text: Connection setup now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh (fetch to login.salesforce.com) plus a prisma.credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where the previous code created the jsforce Connection and let jsforce refresh lazily only when the access token expired. Every booking/availability operation involving Salesforce pays an extra OAuth round-trip and a DB write (concurrent operations also race on credential.update), multiplying Salesforce token-endpoint load and adding latency to a hot path that previously refreshed only on expiry.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then unconditionally updates the DB via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (see the added block starting at `const response = await fetch(...)` through the `prisma.credential.update` call). This is a diff-grounded concern about added latency/load and potential concurrent-update races on a hot path, even if it may not be a functional correctness bug.
